podcast.body: Barbra Streisand recorded her version of "You Don't Bring Me Flowers" and included it on her LP in 1978, approximately six months after Neil Diamond released his. Her recording was an album cut and was not issued as a standalone single. "But flowers, a lament for a fading romance that Neil Diamond himself co-wrote, wasn't issued as a single by him or by Barbara Streisand."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: Following the unexpected radio success of Gary Guthrie's spliced duet, Barbra Streisand joined Neil Diamond in a studio to re-record "You Don't Bring Me Flowers" as an official duet. This collaboration resulted in a number one hit on Billboard's Hot 100 in December 1978. "They went into a studio together, and re-recorded flowers as an actual nose-to-nose duet."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: This song, a duet with Neil Diamond, was a Top 10 contemporary of Gino Vannelli's "I Just Wanna Stop," sharing a similar musical style. "You don't bring me flowers by Barbara"
